Networking problems after the October 2026 Windows update? NTLM might be to blame
item.description: The October 2026 Windows security update may break networking for some customers who are still clinging to long-deprecated NTLMv1 security. A seemingly minor change in the update could have major implications for administrators and enterprises that haven't fully moved away from the legacy technology. Before the October 2026 update, Windows permitted NTLMv1-derived credentials for Single Sign-On and generated warning events. After the update, requests to use NTLMv1-derived credentials are blocked. It comes down to the BlockNtlmSSO registry value. If it hasn't been set, Windows will now use Enforce mode (1) instead of Audit mode (0), thus blocking requests and potentially impacting Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and VPN authentication, and therefore connections. The update does not set the value of BlockNtlmSSO, and administrators can set it to 0 to temporarily allow NTLMv1-derived Single Sign-On credentials. However, Microsoft noted, "Using Audit mode reduces the protection provided by Enforce mode and should only be considered as a scoped, temporary security exception." To be clear, this is not a bug and is by design. The addition of NTLM to the deprecation list occurred in 2024, and Microsoft added audit logs for NTLMv1 usage in late August 2025. The Windows giant has made no secret of its desire to ditch the legacy technology, stating in 2023, "Our end goal is eliminating the need to use NTLM at all." The problem is NTLM's longevity. It appeared in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1, and removing it from enterprise environments has proven tricky, even though it is somewhat insecure by modern standards. Microsoft removed it from Windows 11 24H2 and Windows Server 2025, but some remnants can still be found, notably when using MS-CHAPv2-based connections, including PEAP-MSCHAPv2, and EAP-MSCHAPv2, in a domain-joined environment. Hence the introduction of the audit mode in 2025, to help administrators spot where the technology was still being used. It is now 2026, and Microsoft has taken the next step. If Credential Guard is not enabled and BlockNtlmSSO is not set to Audit mode (0), the use of NTLMv1-derived credentials will be blocked as Microsoft works "to finalize the disablement of NTLMv1." There is no indication of how long the BlockNtlmSSO workaround (setting the value to Audit mode) will work - most likely until the next major Windows release. In September, Microsoft said, "In-market versions of Windows client and Windows Server will continue to support NTLM." However, it also stated, "Our long-term objective is a Windows platform that doesn't need NTLM at all." As such, if the message wasn't already clear, the move to enforce it by default makes it impossible to miss. The technology still exists in the operating system, but it is on its way out and will be removed in a future Windows release. Problems with networking after the October 2026 Windows security update could therefore signal that migration plans are not as far along, or as complete, as administrators mi

item.title: Matchday 31: Messi's MVP form, Texas Derby & Hell is Real!
item.description: Matchday 31: Messi's MVP form, Texas Derby & Hell is Real! By MLSsoccer staff The Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs race continues this weekend with three marquee matchups during Matchday 31. Lionel Messi and Inter Miami CF visit Atlanta United for Walmart Saturday Showdown. Additionally, Houston Dynamo FC host FC Dallas for the Texas Derby and FC Cincinnati welcome Columbus Crew for Hell is Real. Here's what to watch as the regular season enters the home stretch. Download Polymarket : $50 Bonus with code MLS50 Click Here Atlanta United vs. Inter Miami CF Walmart Saturday Showdown WHEN: Saturday, 7:30 pm ET WATCH: Apple TV Inter Miami booked a playoff spot midweek, and now the defending MLS Cup presented by Audi champions can strengthen their hold on the Eastern Conference's No. 2 seed. The Herons, who hope to become the first back-to-back MLS Cup winners since the 2011-12 LA Galaxy , have momentum on their side following two straight wins over D.C. United and New York City FC by a combined 6-0 scoreline. Lionel Messi remains elite as ever and is the odds-on favorite to secure a historic Landon Donovan MLS MVP three-peat . He leads the Golden Boot presented by Audi race with a league-best 37 goal contributions (23g/14a), captaining a star-studded squad that also includes Luis Suárez , Rodrigo De Paul and Casemiro . An upset victory would do wonders for Atlanta's playoff hopes. They're six points below the East's final Wild Card spot with five games left, offering hope to head coach Tata Martino's side. Despite their struggles in 2026, Atlanta have proven they can frustrate Miami. Just as they did in Wednesday's 3-0 victory over CF Montréal , star Designated Players Miguel Almirón and Breel Embolo scored when the Five Stripes held Miami to a 2-2 road draw in early September. What will the Walmart Saturday Showdown stage deliver? Match Trailer | Atlanta United host Inter Miami in high-stakes clash Houston Dynamo FC vs. FC Dallas WHEN: Saturday, 8:30 pm ET WATCH: Apple TV Bragging rights and crucial Western Conference points are on the line when Houston host Dallas for the Texas Derby. First, the rivalry: Saturday's winner claims El Capitán, the trophy awarded annually to the season series victor. Dallas have the edge after winning a wild 4-3 match vs. Houston earlier this year. Second, the playoff implications: Both clubs are Western Conference contenders, and only four points separate Dallas (third place) and Houston (fifth place) in the table. This one is a true "six-pointer," and against a bitter rival no less. Houston will lean on Guilherme , their Brazilian forward who's an MLS Newcomer of the Year contender. He's contributed 16g/9a since arriving from Santos FC during the winter. Dallas are led by Petar Musa , whose 19 goals are second in the Golden Boot race. The Croatian international featured at the 2026 FIFA World Cup this summer and scored an emotional goal against England. FC Cincinnati vs. Columbus Crew Sunday Night Soccer pres. by Continenta

item.title: Coby White believes he is right where he is supposed to be at home with the Hornets
item.description: Coby White believes he is right where he is supposed to be at home with the Hornets originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After multiple years of playing for the Chicago Bulls , Coby White was traded to the Charlotte Hornets . As soon as he got traded, White felt like he jumped back a few years because he grew up in North Carolina and he was back home. He is happy where he is playing because not only is he home close to family, but he is loving his time playing for the Hornets . In fact, he made sure to commit because he signed a three-year deal worth $74 million with the Hornets. Coby White is happy at home with the Hornets White has become the Hornets' new franchise point guard after the LaMelo Ball trade. It seems that he is embracing his new role not only because it's a huge opportunity, but it is also a chance for him to stand out for his hometown team. The current Hornets roster is quite young, so while White is not the oldest player, he is a proven veteran when compared to his younger teammates. He is fully embracing this role as both a veteran-ish player and North Carolina native. MORE: Coby White has stood out as a leader for the Hornets in the 2026 offseason During the 21 games he played for the Hornets in the 2025-26 season, he averaged 15.6 points, three rebounds, and three assists per game coming off the bench. Of course, those numbers are poised to go up now that he is a starting point guard for his team. "I'm right where I'm supposed to be, I'm right where I belong... Being back in NC, it definitely sparked the light inside me. I wouldn't say that I was losing my love and joy for the game, but I was trying to search for it. And when I got here, that lit a spark," White said in the Hornets' latest YouTube video that followed the Hornets' point guard . White is now cemented as one of the Hornets' most important figures. Of course, Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel are crucial players for the Hornets, but someone like White is important for on-court production, off-court activities, and team culture. More NBA news: Brandon Miller gives his honest thoughts about the LaMelo Ball trade The Hornets and Brandon Miller might be running out of time to sign a new contract Grant Williams shares some major news about his family Charles Lee appreciates Naz Reid's contributions since joining the Hornets Naz Reid is already a popular figure in the Hornets' locker room

item.title: Gopher Women’s Hockey Hosts #1 Ohio State Buckeyes in WCHA Clash
item.description: The #3 ranked Minnesota Golden Gophers women’s hockey team will host another leg of the tri-pillars of supremacy in women’s college hockey when the #1 ranked Ohio State Buckeyes come to Ridder Arena this weekend. Both teams are still undefeated on the season with Minnesota sitting at 4-0 and with Ohio State at 6-0. The schedules have looked a bit different however. The Buckeyes opened their season with a sweep of #5 Penn State in Pegula Ince Arena, and then last weekend swept previously #1 and current #2 Wisconsin in Columbus. Meanwhile Minnesota has defeated Bemidji State three times and Maine once. This should be a good test to see just where the Boom May led Gophers sit, and if they can keep things close against the obvious #1 team in the nation early in the season. The Gophers opened their season two weekends ago with a road sweep of Bemidji State with cores of 5-2 and 5-3. They returned home last weekend to host the East/West Showcase at Ridder Arena where they defeated Maine 4-0 before knocking off Bemidji State in a non-conference matchup 4-2 on Sunday. Hanna Clark and Layla Hemp have split the time in net so far this season with each goalie going 2-0. Clark was in net for the shutout of Maine last Friday making 25 saves, and is likely to get the start in game one Friday against the Buckeyes. Offensively defender Molly Jordan is leading the way for the Gophers with five points on two goals and three assists. Freshman and the WCHA Coaches pick for Preseason WCHA Freshman of the Year Adriani Milani leads Minnesota with four goals on the season. On the other side, the Buckeyes are loaded this season. Their international pipeline is paying off as Mira Jungåker and Hilda Svensson are tied for a team-high 11 points on the year. Svensson leads the team with six goals this season and Jungåker has a team-high 10 assists. Minnesota can not afford to take penalties this weekend ad the Buckeyes are deadly on the power play. Ohio State is tied for first nationally with six power play goals on the year and rank second with a .375 power play percentage. The Buckeyes swept the conference Player of the Week awards after their wins over Wisconsin with Jungåker earning WCHA Defender of the Week honors while forward Sanni Vanhanen claimed WCHA Forward of the Week recognition after recording two goals and three points against the Badgers. In net Ohio State appears to have found a freshman phenom in Rowan Houweling. She is 4-0 on the season which included both wins over Wisconsin last weekend earning her WCHA freshman of the Week honors. Minnesota will hope that adding a bit more grit to their team and a new team focused playing style under May can help change the way they play teams like the Buckeyes. While Minnesota holds a 85-34-7 record all-time over Ohio State, things have changed significantly since former Gopher star Nadine Muzerall took over in Columbus. item.title: What is a superficial blood clot? Doctor explains Jalen Hurts' recovery timeline and season outlook
item.description: What is a superficial blood clot? Doctor explains Jalen Hurts' recovery timeline and season outlook originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles are dealing with a serious injury to star quarterback Jalen Hurts. Hurts was ruled out for the Eagles' Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday as he has been diagnosed with a blood clot found in his leg . Hurts has previously been dealing with what the team classified as a calf injury he suffered during Philadelphia's Week 5 game against the Los Angeles Rams . Wednesday leading up to the Panthers' game, he told reporters he got "nicked" against the Rams. Ahead of the Eagles' game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , an ultrasound was performed Saturday after the team flew to London. "The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot," the Eagles said in a statement. "Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia." Hurts was cleared to play against the Jaguars, and did so without limitation. On Wednesday evening after returning from London, another ultrasound revealed "movement" in the blood clot, and Hurts was effectively ruled out. The Sporting News spoke with Dr. Syed T. Zaidi , a vascular surgeon at Orlando Heart Health & Vascular Institute, to learn more about Hurts' diagnosis and recovery. IYER: Why Jalen Hurts' blood clot won't doom 2-3 Eagles' NFC playoff chances What to know about Jalen Hurts' diagnosis and recovery What is Jalen Hurts' diagnosis? Jalen Hurts has been diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his leg, otherwise known as thrombosis. According to the the Harvard Medical School thrombophlebitis is a blood clot (thrombus) inside an inflamed vein. Clots that affect superficial veins, which are seen easily near the surface of the skin — it's called superficial thrombophlebitis. They are common in people who have varicose veins. "The first important thing with these blood clots is to kind of delineate the type of blood clots that they are," Zaidi said. "When you say superficial, in layman's terms, that means it's closer to the surface compared to deep, which is kind of in the deeper veins of the leg. So regarding both, the symptoms are pretty similar in the sense that you'll have swelling, pain, and leg tightness." What is a superficial blood clot vs. deep vein thrombosis? According to Cleveland Clinic , superficial thrombophlebitis occurs in the body's superficial veins, which are closer to the skin. They are considered less serious than deep vein thrombosis, otherwise known as DVT, which forms in the body's deeper veins. item.title: First-Ever NYYC International Women’s Championship Regatta Takes Place In Newport
item.description: Megan Grapengeter-Rudnick’s Team Vigilant were out in front and looking back at the rest of the fleet for most of NYYC's International Women's Championship that was held in Newport, Rhode Island in September ©Paul Todd/OUTSIDEIMAGES.COM Happy Friday everyone! I must admit, after being in the road for most of September and a good chunk of early October, I’m happy to be home, in front of my large screen computer (so, much easier for my aging eyes to see than my laptop), digging out from the backlog of stories that have piled up because I’m not that great at writing on the road. Anyhoo, it’s Friday. The weekend is almost upon us. And I hope you’ll forgive me, but, I’m inspired to write about an event I attended about a month ago because I think the first-ever edition of the New York Yacht Club International Women’s Championship Presented by State Street Investment Management and SPY that took place September 12 to 19 at the New York Yacht Club, Harbour Court in Newport, Rhode Island should be celebrated. Even if I’m a month late! It’s important because the regatta attracted 20 all-women teams from around the world who sailed in the NYYC’s fleet of 37-foot-long IC37 keelboats. The racing was world class. And so was the sponsor list that included founding partner Rolex , regatta sponsor Helly Hansen and official suppliers Tiffany & Co. and Palm Beach Motor Yachts . 20 teams from around the world competed in the International NYYC Women's Championship ©Paul Todd/OUTSIDEIMAGES.COM But I think best thing about the International Women’s Championship is that it brought many of the world’s best female sailors from nearly every high-performance class together in one place for a significant, five-day-long regatta. And lots of teams echoed what Lisa Ross of the Canadian Kairos Racing team said before racing started. “We are excited about racing within the IC37 fleet and the platform it gives our athletes, challenging their teamwork, communication and technical skills. The Championship is creating space for female sailors to excel on and off the water.” That’s exactly what happened. Megan Grapengeter-Rudnick’s Team Vigilant started strong yet looked surprisingly mortal as they battled through a dying breeze for in final three races. Their finishes of sixth, seventh and 10th were their worst of the 10-race regatta. But after four days of immaculate sailing, their last day scores were more than enough to ensure victory in this historic regatta. Team Vigilant wins the NYYC International Women's Championship ©Paul Todd/OUTSIDEIMAGES.COM “When we started the project, the goal was to win this event,” said Stephanie Roble, tactician for Team Vigilant. “But there’s so much that goes into it. Over the last few years, we really focused so much on the process of becoming the best version of ourselves in order to show up here and be the best. It’s been a really rewarding process as a team, and there have been a lot of highs and lows throughout two years of training. We’re

item.title: Banana Ball is coming to Worcester for two games at Polar Park
item.description: The wait is over and "Banana Ball" is coming to Polar Park. The high-energy take on baseball will come to Worcester for two games at Polar Park on Friday, July 30 and Saturday, July 31, 2027. Fans can enter the ticket lottery now through 11:59 p.m. on October 31 at bananaball.com . A random drawing will take place before the event and fans will be contacted via email with directions to purchase available tickets. The game will feature two of the six teams in the Banana Ball Championship League, the Firefighters and the Texas Tailgaters. The Tailgaters defeated the Savannah Bananas, 2-1, to claim the inaugral Banana Bowl Championship earlier this month at Nationals Park in Washington, D.C. Standard tickets start at $35, with Meet & Greet tickets starting at $125. Single game tickets can only be purchased at bananaball.com . For group and hospitality information, visit polarpark.com . The entertainment-first baseball league started in 2018 with the Savannah Bananas and quickly went viral with clips of trick plays and exciting moments. The games feature strict two-hour time limits with unique rules such as no walks, no bunting or mound visits. Fans can also record outs by catching foul balls in the stands as well as other twists on the national pastime. This article originally appeared on Telegram & Gazette: Banana Ball is coming to Worcester for two games at Polar Park

item.title: Colts release NFL veteran before he even plays a game
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts have released an NFL veteran wide receiver before he could make a single appearance for the team, ending a brief stint that lasted less than a month. The Colts have released veteran WR Darius Slayton, the team announced. Indianapolis signed Slayton on September 21, but he never appeared in a game with the Colts. https://t.co/DNaVHLCpqD — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 16, 2026 Darius Slayton, 29, was released by Indianapolis on Friday after signing with the team on September 21. Despite joining the Colts to provide experience and depth to their receiving corps, Slayton never appeared in a regular-season game for the franchise. The move comes as Indianapolis looks to regroup following a challenging start to the season. The Colts are 2-3 heading into Week 6 and will now turn their attention to an important divisional matchup against the winless Tennessee Titans. MORE: Baker Mayfield gives injury update ahead of Week 6 vs Steelers Slayton’s brief stint with Indianapolis comes to an end New York Giants wide receiver Darius Slayton (18) runs with the ball, Sunday, January 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. Slayton initially joined the Colts to provide a veteran presence in the passing game, particularly with Alec Pierce sidelined by a left heel injury. However, the former New York Giants receiver did not play in Weeks 3 or 4 as he continued learning Indianapolis’ offensive system. His opportunity to contribute was further delayed when he was ruled out of Week 5 with a knee injury. Ultimately, Slayton was unable to get on the field before the Colts decided to move on. His release leaves Indianapolis looking elsewhere for additional receiving depth as the team prepares for the second half of the season. For Slayton, the departure marks another setback after a difficult stretch in his NFL career. MORE: Andy Reid chasing NFL history in Week 6 Veteran receiver looks for his next opportunity Dec 1, 2025; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New York Giants wide receiver Darius Slayton (18) catches a pass against New England Patriots cornerback Carlton Davis III (7) for a touchdown during the fourth quarter at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Before joining Indianapolis, Slayton spent the first seven seasons of his NFL career with the Giants, establishing himself as a productive deep threat. He recorded more than 4,400 receiving yards and 22 touchdowns during his time in New York, averaging an impressive 15.0 yards per catch. His ability to stretch the field made him a valuable option in the Giants’ passing attack. However, a core injury suffered toward the end of the 2025 season disrupted his momentum. Slayton was subsequently released by New York at the end of training camp this season before signing with Indianapolis. Now a free agent again, the 29-year-old will look for another opportunity to continue his NFL career. Meanwhile, the Colts will shift their focus to Sunday’s Week 6 showdown against the Tennes

item.title: Eagles signing Cowboys QB Joe Milton to active roster
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Eagles have officially poached a Dallas Cowboys player. Breaking: The #Eagles are signing QB Joe Milton off the #Cowboys practice squad and to their 53-man roster, per sources. pic.twitter.com/e4LVVD4ove — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 16, 2026 It was reported on Friday morning that the Eagles are signing Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton, who was on Dallas’ practice squad, to their 53-man roster. The Cowboys obviously chose not to promote Milton themselves. In case you are unaware, the Eagles were dealt some scary news on Thursday as it was reported that Jalen Hurts is dealing with a “ superficial blood clot. ” He was ruled out of their game this week against the Carolina Panthers and obviously no one knows what the long-term status is there, he was ruled out indefinitely for context . Everyone hopes this is nothing serious or long-term. Joe Milton really impressed in the preseason and there were fans concerned when he initially did not make Dallas’ own 53-man roster. He cleared waivers though and was signed to the practice squad, and again clearly the Cowboys felt like promoting him themselves right now was not an option at this time. Jaydon Blue is currently on the Eagles’ practice squad so they are racking up some former Cowboys offensive players. It is certainly worth mentioning that Dallas visits Philadelphia a week from Monday night.

item.title: MSU AD unbothered by coach's middle finger: 'We're not choir children'
item.description: EAST LANSING — Pat Fitzgerald said he was sorry for flipping the bird. But his new boss said the apology wasn't necessary. Michigan State athletic director Dan Bartholomae, who was standing on the sidelines for most of last week's 38-37 loss to Illinois at Spartan Stadium , said Fitzgerald's passion and enthusiasm are exactly what the football program needs right now from the first-year head coach. "We are not sitting here trying to be choir children," Bartholomae said this week during an interview with The News. "And so, did I have a problem with what Pat did? I did not. I did not. "In fact, I appreciated that got the crowd riled up. I appreciated the crowd's response." With less than 8 minutes to play in last Saturday's game, Michigan State's Samson Gash appeared to have recovered an onside kick. But officials ruled Michigan State was offsides. It was a debatable ruling, and Fitzgerald wasn't having it. As the replay was shown at length on the videoboard at Spartan Stadium, the crowd grew angry, and Fitzgerald leaned into that and egged the fans on, waving his arms toward the stands. He then turned back toward the field of play and gave his one-finger salute to the refs. It was a quick gesture, and, of course, it went viral. Fitzgerald, during his press conference Monday, apologized for that middle finger — “My mom is rolling over in her grave,” he said this week — but not for sticking up for his team. "I think he handled it well," Bartholomae said of Fitzgerald's presser Monday. "I don't anticipate him doing something like that (the middle finger) again. I think he said that himself. He recognizes he got caught up in the moment, and it was a mistake. But, shoot man, I can rally around that fire." Bartholomae said he didn't talk with Fitzgerald about the middle finger until they saw each other at practice Monday. "I told him that had he not brought it up (at the press conference), I probably wouldn't have even said anything," Bartholomae said. "That's the kind of energy that I want. "I think you have to have a little bit of fire in your belly." Officials' call of offsides on the onside kick recovery wasn't able to be challenged by Fitzgerald, but Michigan State still rallied to tie the game and send it to overtime. In OT, Illinois scored first and kicked the extra point. Then, Michigan State responded with a touchdown, but opted to go for the two-point conversion and the win, rather than a tie and another OT. The conversion failed and MSU lost to fall to 2-4 on the season. Bartholomae also liked seeing Fitzgerald go for the win. "I'm like, s***, I'm so glad he did," Bartholomae said. "We're going to be edge ... and be OK with that. "Everybody's going to have to be OK with that." Michigan State plays Northwestern, Fitzgerald's former school , at noon Saturday at Spartan Stadium. tpaul@detroitnews.com @tonypaul1984 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: MSU AD unbothered by coach's middle finger: 'We're not choir children'

item.title: What to Know About the Blood Clot Sidelining Jalen Hurts
item.description: Jalen Hurts of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London. —DeFodi Images—Getty Images For an NFL quarterback, a sore calf might seem like an unsurprising consequence of getting hit by a cleat. In Jalen Hurts ’ case, an ultrasound revealed something else: a superficial blood clot. The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback was struck in the calf during an Oct. 4 game and sought treatment four days later, according to a statement from the team. An ultrasound in London revealed the clot, but doctors cleared him to play in the team’s game there the next day. Then, a follow-up ultrasound Wednesday night revealed “movement in the small blood clot.” The Eagles announced Thursday that Hurts would miss Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers while the team determines his treatment. What makes a clot superficial—and when does it become dangerous? We asked doctors to explain. What’s the difference between a superficial clot and deep vein thrombosis? To understand blood clots, picture a road map. Your deep veins run within the muscles of your arms and legs, carrying most of the blood returning from your limbs to your heart. Superficial veins sit closer to the surface, just underneath the skin and in the tissue beneath it. Connecting veins bridge the two systems. “You have a really well interconnected network of veins,” says Dr. William Shutze, a vascular surgeon at Texas Vascular Associates in Dallas and vice president of the Society for Vascular Surgery (who was not involved in Hurts’ care). Think of it as “a very well developed road and highway system,” with multiple routes to get where you need to go. When a clot blocks one route, blood can take a detour through other veins. A superficial clot forms in one of the veins near the skin. The area can become red, warm, and tender. “It’s usually very uncomfortable,” Shutze says. Some develop in varicose veins; others form where a needle or IV has irritated a vein. You can sometimes feel the affected vein beneath your fingers. “It’s like a pencil underneath the skin, or a knot,” says Dr. Stephan Moll, a hematologist and professor of medicine at the University of North Carolina who runs an Athletes and Blood Clots Clinic (who was not involved in Hurts’ care). Deep vein thrombosis involves a clot farther inside the body. Its symptoms can be more widespread—the whole calf or ankle might become swollen and painful, Moll says. You can’t feel the deep vein itself. Many superficial clots stay put and get better without blood thinners. But sometimes, a clot grows into one of the deeper veins. A piece can then break off and travel to the lungs, causing a potentially life-threatening complication called a pulmonary embolism. Doctors use ultrasound to assess the clot and check for deep-vein involvement, Shutze says. They’re particularly concerned about superficial clots longer than 5 centimeters or withi

item.title: Blackburn Rovers could be boosted by key man’s return against West Brom
item.description: Blackburn Rovers could be boosted by key man’s return against West Brom Scott Wharton could make his long-awaited return to the Blackburn Rovers matchday squad against West Bromwich Albion this weekend, Tony Mowbray has revealed. The defender has not featured for the first team this season after suffering an injury in pre-season, but has now come through successive Under-21s appearances without a problem. His latest outing came against Bolton Wanderers B earlier this week, leaving Mowbray with a decision to make ahead of Saturday’s trip to The Hawthorns. “Scotty Wharton’s going to join the group, although we’re undecided whether he’s going to be involved or not, but it’s great that he played for the Under-21s,” Mowbray said. “He might need another week or so of training with the intensity that we train at, but it’s good to have him back and the numbers are increasing all the time.”

item.title: Eagles saw backup QB in huddle before learning Jalen Hurts news: ‘What’s going on?’
item.description: PHILADELPHIA — When Eagles right guard Tyler Steen walked onto the practice field for Thursday’s walkthrough session, he saw backup quarterback Tanner McKee getting ready to go into the huddle. Prior to that point, Steen was not told by the team that quarterback Jalen Hurts was out for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers with a small superficial blood clot. “We were like, ‘Oh, what’s going on?’” Steen told NJ.com on Thursday. Steen said after seeing McKee in the huddle, the news of Hurts’ injury spread around the team. That’s when they learned that Hurts would not be playing against the Panthers. “It was surprising,” Steen said. “We were in the middle of a work day to prepare for the Panthers.” Steen said that he saw Hurts around the building after the walkthrough. “He was in good spirits,” Steen said. The Eagles announced the Hurts’ news at 1:02 p.m., more than an hour after the walkthrough began. RELATED : Update: Eagles vs. Panthers odds swing massively on Kalshi off news of Hurts’ injury MORE BY CAYDEN STEELE Eagles blindsided by Jalen Hurts news as things go from bad to worse: ‘Is this real?’ Oct. 16, 2026, 6:12 a.m. Eagles’ Jalen Hurts is ‘out indefinitely’: 5 outside options to replace him, including ex-Philly QB Oct. 16, 2026, 9:04 a.m. Steen said Thursday’s session started around noon. It’s unclear how long Hurts will be out for this season. His injury adds to a long list of issues. “It sounds serious,” Steen said about the blood clot. “And fortunately, it seems like he’s in good spirits. I don’t know how serious it is or the situation. It’s unfortunate that he has to deal with that.” Read the original article on NJ.com . Add NJ.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: San Francisco 49ers reporter accused of hugging players in locker room
item.description: Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan hasn’t always been the biggest fan of Grant Cohn’s questions , but that’s part of life on the beat. According to Cohn, David Lombardi didn’t get that memo. “I can’t stand David Lombardi,” said Cohn, a reporter for 49ers On SI, on his postgame livestream last Sunday. “It’s bad enough that he’s a fan of the team that he covers, but he thinks he’s on the team. So, for example, after a game, you might hear some of us interviewing players and the coach at the postgame press conference. You know who never asks a question? Dave Lombardi. You know why? Because he’s not in there. You know why? Because he’s in the locker room. You know what he’s doing? Hugging the players!” Cohn said that Lombardi, who covers the 49ers for the San Francisco Standard, celebrates with the 49ers “as if they won together” and grew increasingly visibly irritated at Lombardi’s alleged behavior. “It does bother me,” Cohn said. “They say before you go in the locker room, ‘If you’re not in here conducting interviews, you have to leave.’ He’s hugging the players! […] You’re a player on the 49ers. You just won, [and] you’re celebrating with your brothers. Here comes this freaking guy to give you a hug as if you guys accomplished something together. Who the f*ck are you?” As any journalist knows — or should know, though lines are blurrier than ever in sports media now — “it’s not your job to bro out with the players,” Cohn said. Cohn conceded that he would hug 49ers All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner if he ran into him at San Francisco International Airport in the offseason. He’d even hug Shanahan at the annual NFL league meeting. But he said there must be a “professional distance” during the season. “I don’t give Kyle a hug in the locker room after the game and say, ‘How’d it feel? How’s it feel to be 5-0?’ Man, f*ck that!” Cohn said. “I’m sorry, dude. I do disapprove of fans covering teams, but still, Brian Nemhauser is a fan of the Seahawks. He does a great job, even though he’s a fan of the team. He doesn’t think he’s on the team, and he holds their team accountable. This f*cking guy pretends to be a journalist and takes shilling to the next level.” Alex Simon of SFGATE reached out to the San Francisco Standard for comment on Cohn’s allegations, but editor-in-chief Kevin Delaney declined. Neither Cohn nor Lombardi responded to Simon’s request for comment. The post San Francisco 49ers reporter accused of hugging players in locker room appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Rutgers Opponent Q&A w/ Maryland’s Testudo Times
item.description: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 8: Bo Mascoe #3 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights forces a fumble from Jalil Farooq #1 of the Maryland Terrapins during the first half at SHI Stadium on November 8, 2025 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Rutgers matchup against Maryland is viewed on both sides of the aisle as one of the few realistic opportunities to get a Big Ten win by both teams. With both teams having coaches on the hot seat and having four losses, we wanted to do a check-in on our bottom of the Big Ten brothers. Below is a list of questions that we had answered by Nolan Rogalski, a reporter for SB Nation’s Testudo Times, on the status of Maryland football and their views on their upcoming matchup with the Scarlet Knights. 1. What is your strongest position group on offense? Maryland’s strongest offensive position group… is a difficult question to answer. Before the season, I would’ve told you without a second thought that Malik Washington is the best player on this team. But that hasn’t been the case fully… more on that later. For now, I’ll say it’s the tight end room, which has two legitimate NFL prospects in Dorian Fleming and Preston Howard. However, both of these guys have been injured at times during the season, and whether it’s because of that or something else, they have not been as notable a part of the passing or run-blocking game as I would have expected. Combined with some useful depth pieces, it’s the best of a less-than-ideal bunch, though. One of Maryland’s biggest issues this season has been its lack of depth just about everywhere. The Terps have suffered a lot of injuries this season and have clearly lost a step talent-wise. 2. What is your strongest position group on defense? Maryland’s strongest defensive position group is undoubtedly its defensive ends — even with a 2025 freshman all-Big Ten player in Zahir Mathis out for the year. Sidney Stewart is probably the singular most important piece for Maryland on defense, he will command double-teams constantly and still get home to the quarterback a couple times a game. His stats are down because of it, but it gives room for his opposite number to work as well, whether that be five-star freshman Zion Elee — who’s grown into a role on this defense and has the talent to play somewhere far better than Maryland next year — or sophomores DD Holmes and Nahsir Taylor, who form a legitimate four-man platoon on the edge that has the ability to keep quarterbacks honest. It’s also freed up Maryland’s interior defensive linemen, which is a group that has definitely improved from last year. However, Maryland’s edge is much better against the pass than the run, the Terps will likely have quite a few problems stopping Antwan Raymond. 3. How has Malik Washington developed from his freshman to sophomore year? Malik Washington was incredibly talented but very raw as a freshman. item.title: The Eagles let this $120 million free agent walk. Now, they’re facing him
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles let one of their best defensive players walk in free agency seven months ago. Now, on Sunday, the Eagles will have to try to stop him — while still trying to replace his impact. Jaelan Phillips will make his return to Philadelphia on Sunday when the Eagles host the Carolina Panthers. Phillips, the dynamic 27-year-old edge rusher, spent half a season with the Eagles. Howie Roseman dealt a third-round pick to the Miami Dolphins at the trade deadline to bring in the 2021 first-round pick on an expiring contract. Almost a year ago, Phillips said getting traded to the Eagles was the “best thing that’s ever happened” to him in his life. Eight games — and 41 QB pressures, four passes defended and two sacks — later, he was gone. The Eagles couldn’t retain Phillips. He would have been a perfect fit to stay in Philadelphia long-term given his age profile, production and familiarity with defensive coordinator Vic Fangio. The two worked together in Miami in 2023. But the Eagles got outbid. There was reported “optimism” around Phillips coming back. But the Panthers signed him to a four-year, $120 million deal with $80 million guaranteed — more than what Roseman was willing to offer. “Some of the negatives to letting your players walk in free agency is ... there are highest bidders,” Roseman said in the spring . “At some point, you’ve got to have parameters of what you would do, what you wouldn’t do.” Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jaelan Phillips (50) in action against Las Vegas Raiders offensive tackle Stone Forsythe (70) during the first half of an NFL football game, Sunday, Dec. 14, 2025, in Philadelphia.. (AP Photo/Terrance Williams) AP Phillips’ $30 million average annual salary ranked second among 2026 free agent signings behind only Los Angeles Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie ($31 million). Keeping Phillips required a hefty investment. The Eagles tried to replace Phillips by trading for Jonathan Greenard in April. Greenard, the 2024 Pro Bowler, was acquired from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for two third-round picks. The Eagles ended up giving Greenard a four-year deal worth $98 million ($50 million guaranteed). The Eagles hoped Greenard — plus young edge rushers Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith — would be enough to form a fearsome pass rush and pressure the quarterback. It hasn’t panned out that way. The Eagles have six sacks; only two teams who have played five games have fewer. And the Eagles’ pass-rush win rate (44%) ranks 28th in the NFL. Hunt’s dominant summer didn’t translate before suffering ankle and knee injuries vs. the Jaguars on Sunday. Smith has flashed at times. And Greenard, after missing all of training camp due to injury, has played in only two games. Greenard missed the first two games of the season with a pec strain, exited the Week 4 loss to the Rams with an ankle injury and couldn’t go against the Jaguars in London. Greenard practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday, so we’ll see about his availability this

item.title: Packers Legend Aaron Rodgers in Rare Company Among All-Time QBs
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - JANUARY 08: Aaron Rodgers #12 of the Green Bay Packers warms up prior to the game against the Detroit Lions at Lambeau Field on January 08, 2023 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 01: Quarterbacks Aaron Rodgers #12 (R) of the Green Bay Packers and Peyton Manning #18 (L) of the Denver Broncos talk while surrounded by media after the Broncos 29-10 win at Sports Authority Field at Mile High on November 1, 2015 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Getty ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 08: Head coach Todd Bowles of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers looks on prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 08, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty Former Green Bay Packers quarterback Aaron Rodgers continues to rewrite the NFL record book in what he has said will be his final season. The 42-year-old has officially moved ahead of Peyton Manning for third place on the NFL’s all-time list for career touchdown passes when postseason games are included. Rodgers broke the tie during the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 34-22 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11. His 580th career touchdown pass came on an 80-yard catch-and-run by Jaylen Warren in the first quarter. Rodgers, tied with Manning at 579 prior to the bout, didn’t stop after passing the Hall of Famer. The former UC Berkeley added two touchdown passes to Pat Freiermuth to finish the victory with 582 career scores, postseason included. Rodgers Leaves Manning Behind Getty DENVER, CO – NOVEMBER 01: Quarterbacks Aaron Rodgers #12 (R) of the Green Bay Packers and Peyton Manning #18 (L) of the Denver Broncos talk while surrounded by media after the Broncos 29-10 win at Sports Authority Field at Mile High on November 1, 2015 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Rodgers now trails only Tom Brady and Drew Brees on the career touchdown list when playoff numbers are included. Brady sits comfortably atop the list with 737. Brees finished his career with 608. NFL.com noted after the milestone that Rodgers also joined Brady, Brees and Manning as the only quarterbacks with at least 90 games featuring three or more touchdown passes. Rodgers has thrown at least three touchdown passes in three consecutive games for the first time since his 2021 MVP campaign in Green Bay. That hot streak has also put him into rare Steelers company. Per the Associated Press , Rodgers is the first Pittsburgh quarterback to throw three touchdown passes in three straight games since Terry Bradshaw in 1982. Rodgers’ career stats are heavily connected to his 18 seasons with the Packers. He won all four of his NFL MVP awards in Green Bay, guided the franchise to a Super Bowl championship and earned 10 Pro Bowl selections during his Packers tenure. item.title: Terry Bradshaw’s Bourbon Business Got Sacked. Now He's Fighting Back
item.description: Football legend Terry Bradshaw with a bottle of his Bradshaw Bourbon. John Hafner Photography Terry Bradshaw knows a thing or two about getting knocked down. During his 14 seasons quarterbacking the Pittsburgh Steelers, he took plenty of hard hits on his way to four Super Bowl championships. He also learned that winning often comes down to getting back up and surrounding yourself with the right people. Now, more than forty years after hanging up his cleats, Bradshaw is calling the plays in a whole new arena: bourbon . His Bradshaw Bourbon brand, launched in 2020, got off to a promising start before significant internal business problems effectively knocked it out of the game. The whiskey largely disappeared from store shelves for roughly two years, leaving Bradshaw frustrated but unwilling to walk away. Now 78, he’s rebuilding the company alongside his wife Tammy, son-in-law Noah Hester and Atlanta-based Tag Reserve Spirits. This time, he’s focused on building a sustainable business rather than chasing rapid expansion or a lucrative celebrity spirits buyout. And he’s not above giving sales a little personal boost. During our conversation, Bradshaw laughingly admitted that he occasionally walks into liquor stores and buys bottles of his own bourbon. On one visit to a store in Gainesville, Texas, he learned that only three bottles remained on the shelf. He bought two and left the third behind. “That way they’ll, they can say, ‘Yeah, it’s moving off the shelf,’” he told me, laughing. “Well, I just bought two of them.” It’s an amusing admission from one of football’s most recognizable personalities, but it also illustrates how personally involved he remains in the business. Bradshaw isn’t content to put his name on a bottle and hope it sells. He’s making calls, visiting retailers and doing whatever he can to help the brand gain traction. “We’re building a company. We’re not building an image here of a celebrity,” Bradshaw said. A Bourbon Brand Born Almost By Accident Unlike most celebrity spirits brands that start with a slick business pitch or a licensing deal, Bradshaw Bourbon’s story begins with a charity fundraiser and a single barrel of Four Roses whiskey. Bradshaw and his wife had been offered the opportunity to purchase a barrel of Four Roses. Tammy enjoyed the whiskey, but Bradshaw wasn’t particularly fond of it. Instead, they arranged to sell the bottles for $100 each at a Florida restaurant, with Bradshaw signing them and the proceeds going to Wounded Warriors. The event sold out, and they repeated the fundraiser the following year. But Bradshaw couldn’t help but wonder—why was he out there hyping someone else’s bourbon, especially one he didn’t even like to drink? “Why are we promoting Four Roses? I don’t even like this blend. Why don’t we see if we can get our own bourbon?” he recalled asking his wife. Bradshaw Bourbon's six-year aged flagship bourbon. item.title: 5 NFL Stars Who Need to Get Back on Track
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor The 2026 NFL season is still in its early stages, but several big-name players have already fallen short of expectations. Whether it’s injuries, inconsistent performances, or struggling offenses, some of the league’s most talented players haven’t made the impact their teams were hoping for. 5 NFL Stars Who Need to Get Back on Track While there’s still plenty of football left to play, the pressure is beginning to mount. Some teams are already facing the possibility of a lost season, while others need their biggest playmakers to step up to remain competitive. Here are five NFL stars who need to get back on track as the season progresses. Justin Herbert, Los Angeles Chargers It’s been a disastrous start for the Chargers, who find themselves sitting at 0-5 despite entering the season with playoff aspirations. Herbert has been flat-out bad through the first five games, throwing seven interceptions and struggling to find any consistency. However, the Chargers’ injury-riddled offensive line hasn’t done him any favors, with Herbert already being sacked 17 times. Still, Herbert deserves his share of the blame. The quarterback has struggled to find his rhythm under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, and the two have yet to establish a functioning offensive system. At this point, Los Angeles may already be facing a lost season. Herbert is among the NFL stars who need to get back on track, and he and McDaniel must show some offensive progress moving forward, even if the playoffs are no longer realistic. Oct 11, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) is pressured by Denver Broncos defensive end Zach Allen (99) during the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images Saquon Barkley, Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are approaching panic mode following a disappointing 2-3 start, and their struggling rushing attack has played a significant role. Barkley hasn’t looked like the dominant running back Philadelphia has grown accustomed to seeing. Injuries and inconsistent offensive line play have contributed to his struggles, but the Eagles desperately need their superstar running back to rediscover his form. With DeVonta Smith battling hamstring and toe injuries and A.J. Brown no longer on the roster, Philadelphia is also dealing with limited receiving depth. Without an effective ground game, the Eagles’ offense becomes increasingly predictable, putting additional pressure on Jalen Hurts and an already depleted passing attack. Once Barkley returns from his hamstring injury , he’ll be another of the NFL stars who need to get back on track to help their teams remain competitive. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Rome Odunze, Chicago Bears The Bears invested heavily in Odunze when they selected him ninth overall in the 2024 NFL Draft, but consistency remains an issue. item.title: Gresini: New MotoGP rules won't increase gap between factory and satellite teams
item.description: Motorsport photo Gresini is confident that the competitive order between factory and satellite teams will remain “more or less” unchanged in 2027, when MotoGP enters its new 850cc era. The championship is set for its biggest technical overhaul in recent history next year, with reduced engine capacity, stricter limits placed on aerodynamics and ride-height devices being outlawed. The switch from Michelin to Pirelli tyres will further add to the complexity, marking a complete generation shift in the technical package. Given the extent of changes, any data gathered from track testing will be valuable in understanding the new bikes and extracting the maximum performance out of them. Some manufacturers began testing their 850cc bikes as early as December last year, before ramping up the development work in recent months. While the new regulations pose a major challenge for the manufacturers themselves, their satellite teams also face a tough task in learning the new bikes and tyres as quickly as possible. With all private testing and the official Brno test in June being restricted to manufacturers themselves, satellite teams had to wait until last month’s Spielberg test to get their hands on the new machines shod with Pirelli tyres. But Ducati customer Gresini has dismissed concerns about new regulations potentially leaving satellite teams on the back foot, with sporting director Michele Masini saying they could even gain an early edge over the factories through their understanding of the new Pirelli tyres. “I think that the level could be more or less the same as now,” Masini told Motorsport.com. “In terms of performance, it will be crucial to immediately understand the Pirelli tyres. One of the most important things in a race is to manage the tyres, depending on which bike you're riding. “In this case, the satellite teams can also play better compared to some factory teams. If you understand immediately how it works and how to manage it, it could be a big help especially for the first couple of races.” Michele Masini, Team Manager, Gresini Racing Michele Masini, Team Manager, Gresini Racing While such a major rule change could increase satellite teams’ reliance on their manufacturer partners, Gresini says it will continue to receive the same level of technical support from Ducati. “I think the support never changes. You don't have to change the support because at the end we work together tirelessly every day of every GP weekend,” Masini said. “I think that I'm really confident that Ducati will put on track a very good package for the riders. But as I said, it will be the same collaboration. “Of course, the character of the bike will change. It will also depend on the character of the tyres.” With the new regulations effectively resetting the field, Masini sees the change as a major opportunity for Gresini, which has won a grand prix every year since its split from Aprilia five years ago. “I'm really excited about that,” he said. “Because every time

item.title: Lakers reportedly in trade talks to send Dalton Knecht to Bucks for ex-Knicks rim-runner
item.description: Lakers reportedly in trade talks to send Dalton Knecht to Bucks for ex-Knicks rim-runner originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers are looking for a way to keep Dalton Knecht from being waived before Wednesday, and the situation could go down to the wire. The Lakers were once excited about drafting Knecht, but things have quickly changed. During his rookie season, the former Tennessee Volunteer got off to a scorching start and was even considered a potential Rookie of the Year candidate. Now, he could be included in a consolidation trade. “My understanding is a consolidation trade. Obviously, it would be two-for-one, three-for-one, or three-for-two is a little more complicated," Lakers insider Jovan Buha said."So I think the most straightforward one would be two-for-one…And depending on the configuration of the trade, it could be a version of two of the back-end guys, let's say Dalton Knecht and Jaden Hardy, for a backup center." LA has been trying to find a trade partner for Knecht. “Have heard the Bucks , Lakers and Grizzlies all exploring trades. Hornets have to weigh the locker room value of retaining Pat Connaughton,” NBA insider Jake Fischer posted. The Lakers are trying to find a trade partner before waiving Knecht forces them to pay a portion of his salary. Fischer reported in The Stein Line on Thursday night that Los Angeles has held talks with the Milwaukee Bucks about a potential deal involving Knecht and Jericho Sims. “League sources say that the Lakers and Bucks have held exploratory trade discussions on a framework that would ship former first-round selection Dalton Knecht to Milwaukee (along with second-round draft capital) in exchange for big man Jericho Sims,” Fischer wrote. This would be exactly what the Lakers have been looking for as they attempt to trade Knecht. Los Angeles knows it needs additional depth at center, especially in case Walker Kessler or Kevon Looney suffers an injury. The deal could benefit both sides, particularly with the Bucks seemingly entering a rebuilding phase. Both teams would acquire players who could potentially fill roles during the season. item.title: Erling Haaland ‘needs some rest’ as Enzo Maresca considers Man City rotation
item.description: Enzo Maresca will consider resting Erling Haaland over the coming weeks as Manchester City balance a busy schedule. Haaland has already racked up 13 starts for club and country this season after playing four times for Norway in the international break. Premier League leaders City host Ipswich on Saturday after Haaland scored twice in the 4-2 home defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday. City will then return to Champions League action against AEK Athens on Tuesday and Maresca said he will need to rotate his squad at some stage. “At some point we probably need to give him rest, some days off,” Maresca said in his pre-match press conference before facing Ipswich. “We are thinking about this not just with Erling because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams. “Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernandez], Marc [Guehi], Erling, Ruben [Dias]. So at some point we probably need to give them some rest.” Haaland took his scoring tally for the season to 10 with his brace against PSG, which made him City’s record Champions League goalscorer. City have won all six of their Premier League games this season can continue their winning start against newly promoted Ipswich. It will be the club’s first home game in the Premier League since they were found guilty of almost all of the Premier League charges. City have maintained their innocence and are appealing the verdict.

item.title: Eagles blindsided by Jalen Hurts news as things go from bad to worse: ‘Is this real?’
item.description: PHILADELPHIA — On Thursday afternoon, Eagles players wondered why Jalen Hurts was not on the field for their walkthrough session. After it was over, they learned why. Hurts was ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers with a blood clot, and his recovery could take a long time depending on the severity. NFL Network reported Hurts is “out indefinitely.” “After walkthrough today, grabbed my phone, and I went on Instagram,” Eagles rookie offensive tackle Markel Bell told NJ.com on Thursday about how he found out about Hurts. “The first thing I saw was, ‘Breaking news: J Hurts out.’ Like, what’s going on? Like, is this real?” When Eagles right guard Tyler Steen walked onto the practice field for Thursday’s walkthrough session, he saw backup quarterback Tanner McKee getting ready to go into the huddle. Prior to that point, Steen was not told by the team that Hurts was out for the Panthers game. “We were like, ‘What’s going on?’” Steen told NJ.com on Thursday. Hurts’ absence is a crushing blow with the team already falling apart. RELATED : Update: Eagles vs. Panthers odds swing massively on Kalshi off news of Hurts’ injury The Eagles had 24 players listed on Wednesday’s injury report, and Hurts being ruled out for the foreseeable future only makes things worse. McKee will start on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers and could start more games if Hurts misses an extended period of time. “Can’t control that,” Eagles offensive tackle Jordan Mailata said about the uncertainty surrounding Hurts’ status this season. “Again, it’s just about preparing the next man up. Preparing whoever our depth chart is. O-line and QB and wide receivers and running backs and tight ends. Just keeping it going, man. You have to have high energy when you face adversity. You have to have positive energy because again, you can either react to it or you can respond. And I’m choosing to respond with a plan of action, a plan of positivity and keeping it going.” Mailata wants to be positive, but he also knows the challenge ahead is extremely difficult. Philadelphia’s roster has become thin, especially after right tackle Lane Johnson retired last week and left guard Cam Jurgens got traded to the Baltimore Ravens. After the Eagles’ loss to the Jaguars last Sunday in London, Mailata called it “the week from hell.” MORE BY CAYDEN STEELE Eagles’ Jalen Hurts is ‘out indefinitely’: 5 outside options to replace him, including ex-Philly QB Oct. 16, 2026, 9:04 a.m. Eagles saw backup QB in huddle before learning Jalen Hurts news: ‘What’s going on?’ Oct. 15, 2026, 6:18 p.m. “Think I was a little early,” Mailata said on Thursday about “the week from hell” statement. “I might have jumped the gun on that one. Holy cow. It’s the NFL. It’s a gift that keeps on giving.” Bell said “it hurts” to see many of his teammates injured, but he’s trying to stay focused on beating the Panthers. “My family members have had a history with blood clots,” Bell said. “I don’t know the severity of it, b

item.title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker reveals what fans don’t see about Patrick Mahomes
item.description: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker reveals what fans don’t see about Patrick Mahomes appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kenneth Walker is arguably the best running back in the NFL right now . The reigning Super Bowl MVP has had a hot start to the 2026 season in his first year with the Kansas City Chiefs , leading the league in rushing with 537 yards. Walker has been the perfect fit in Andy Reid’s offense, while also alleviating a lot of pressure that Patrick Mahomes has had to deal with. On any given week, Walker could be the main option, or it could be Mahomes. For example, in the season-opening win over the Denver Broncos, it was Walker who was the main piece, rushing for 177 yards and two touchdowns on eight yards per attempt. However, in a win over the Indianapolis Colts during the following week, it was Mahomes who was the main option, throwing for nearly 400 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. While Walker is extremely complimentary of Mahomes and his play on the field, he’s big with his praise when it comes to the three-time Super Bowl champion’s personality off the field. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I would just say his personality,” said Walker of Mahomes of what people don’t know much about when it comes to the star quarterback. “You always see him probably intense in the games and everything, but his personality, the way he jokes around with everybody, the type of person he is off the field. I feel like that’s the biggest thing that people don’t see, but I feel like that’s one of my favorite things about him is how he goes about everything and just his personality in general.” Mahomes has shown some of his personality off the field with his quirky nature in State Farm commercials — he stars in them with Andy Reid — and during appearances as one of the NFL’s highest-profile players. The 31-year-old quarterback is coming off a serious season-ending ACL injury last year , but has shown no signs of rust. Mahomes has nine touchdowns against two interceptions while leading the Chiefs to a 4-0 record to start the season. “It’s definitely impressive,” said Walker of Mahomes’ elite play in return from injury. “Injuries like that can take a long time. But when I watched him in OTAs and training camp, the rehab, the early mornings. He would get up early and be at the facility. Probably one of the first guys at the facility. It’s not a surprise because he’s put himself in that position to be able to come out and be able to play at a high level the way he is.” Kansas City is entering the bye week as one of three remaining undefeated teams — the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings being the others — in the NFL. They’ll need Walker and Mahomes’ complementary play to continue their hot start to the season. They’ll take on the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6 before facing Walker’s former team, the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7 in a highly anticipated Sunday Night Football mat

item.title: NCAA sues Gov. DeWine over state executive order on fifth-year eligibility
item.description: The NCAA filed a federal lawsuit against Gov. Mike DeWine, rebuffing an executive order he signed earlier this week allowing student athletes from the Class of 2022 to have a fifth year of eligibility and claiming the governor is giving Ohio universities "a hall pass to break the rules." The 41-page lawsuit was filed Oct. 15 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio. In it, the NCAA condemns DeWine's executive order as a "misguided attempt" to give Ohio universities an "unfair, unprecedented and unwarranted competitive advantage." Ohio State 5th year eligibility: Ohio State not expected to be impacted by order granting 5th year of eligibility It also asks a judge declare that DeWine's executive order violated the U.S. constitution, rule that it has no "force of law," and prohibit the governor under federal and state law from any enforcement of the order. DeWine signed an executive order on Oct. 13 granting a year of availability for the upcoming year to all players who seek to play in the state even if they had previously exhausted their eligibility under previous NCAA rules, prevents Ohio colleges from enforcing eligibility restrictions imposed by the NCAA. The move comes as programs, particularly in men's and women's basketball, are finalizing rosters amid the ongoing uncertainty around new rules permitting five years of eligibility to all players who were already slated to be eligible under the prior, four-year landscape. That meant players from the class of 2022 who finished the 2025-26 season having exhausted their four-year eligibility clock were excluded. There are some exceptions in DeWine's order. A student-athlete has to be within five years of their 19th birthday and five years of enrolling in college as of the start of the 2026-27 academic year, had to be eligible at the end of their last season of competition and did not participate in a professional sports league. A few hours after DeWine's order was issued, NCAA President Charlie Baker distributed a memo acquired and published by ESPN that disputes his authority to do so. "The Governor of Ohio cannot legislate NCAA eligibility rules," it states. "One elected official seeking to make their own rules for their own schools' advantage is a terrible way to run athletic competitions and precisely why Congress must pass the (Protect College Sports Act) as soon as possible." This story will be updated. Dispatch reporter Adam Jardy contributed to this article. Higher education reporter Sheridan Hendrix can be reached at shendrix@dispatch.com and on Signal at @sheridan.120. You can follow her on Instagram at @sheridanwrites. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: NCAA sues Gov. DeWine over state executive order on fifth-year eligibility

item.title: 7 best places to see the northern lights, according to an aurora chaser
item.description: null I've spent years chasing the northern lights across the Arctic, from the mountains of Swedish Lapland to the dramatic Norwegian fjords. If there's one thing I've learned, it's that choosing where to see the northern lights is about much more than simply heading as far north as possible. Whether you're on the hunt for somewhere that offers the best chance of clear skies, the most dramatic scenery or a plethora of winter activities to keep you warm, choosing the right destination can make a big difference, especially as auroras are never guaranteed. My biggest piece of advice? Choose somewhere you've always wanted to visit regardless of whether the northern lights might appear. That way, the auroras become the icing on the cake rather than the sole measure of a successful trip. From my personal favorites in Scandinavia to some of North America's most established aurora hotspots, here are seven of the best places to see the northern lights this 2026/27 season. Best places to see the northern lights at a glance Best places to see the northern lights at a glance Location Best for Kiruna and Abisko, Sweden Best for a short northern lights trip Tromsø, Norway Best for a city break Norwegian coast Best for a scenic Arctic voyage Finnish Lapland Best for a winter wonderland getaway Iceland Best for volcanoes, glaciers and natural wonders Fairbanks, Alaska Best for a U.S. aurora getaway Yellowknife, Canada Best for a Canadian aurora getaway Abisko and Kiruna, Sweden: Best for a short northern lights trip Northern lights from Mount Nuolja, Abisko, Sweden. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) Best time to visit: September to early April Swedish Lapland holds a particularly special place in my heart. It's where I saw the northern lights for the very first time, during a trip to Kiruna in February 2023. I'd only booked two nights in Kiruna, one of which included a northern lights tour with Anders from Outdoor North 67º . Talk about putting all your eggs in one basket! But the gamble paid off, and I was treated to a spellbinding display of auroras dancing across the Arctic sky. I've been hooked ever since. Kiruna offers a wide range of accommodation, restaurants and activities, making it a convenient base for exploring the region. From here, you can join guided aurora tours, visit the famous Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi or head into the wilderness for dog sledding and snowmobiling adventures. One of the region's biggest draws is Abisko National Park, around 60 miles (100 kilometers) northwest of Kiruna. Abisko is famous for its so-called "Blue Hole" , a local weather phenomenon in which the skies above the national park can be clear, even if the surrounding region (and weather forecast) is cloudy. This is partly thanks to the surrounding mountains, which create a rain shadow effect, reducing the precipitation in the area. Glacial-carved valley Lapporten, in Abisko National Park. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic) And if you're visiting Abisko, I'd highly recommend ta

item.title: NTT Global Data Centers weighs the price tag of not building fast enough
item.description: The next 200-megawatt data center permitted in your county probably won't look like the buildings you remember from a decade ago. It will occupy the footprint of two or three football fields and draw more power than most nearby industrial parks combined. It will also likely trigger a town hall meeting before the first pad is poured. That collision between AI-driven demand and physical reality is what NTT Global Data Centers set out to quantify in its new AI Stress Test Report. The report models three growth trajectories through 2030 and stress-tests each against the constraints operators hit, such as land availability, water consumption, specialized labor and more. The middle (baseline) scenario projects annual demand growth of about 23 percent, which pencils out to roughly $3.8 trillion of additional investment in digital infrastructure. Ramp to the accelerated case and the figure climbs to $5.7 trillion. Bruno Berti, CTO at NTT Global Data Centers, notes that he has watched the size envelope stretch beyond recognition. "We used to build ten-megawatt buildings, smaller buildings, to support some of these applications," says Berti. "But now we're building buildings that are hundreds of megawatts, double the size, sizes of two, maybe sometimes three football fields." Why permitting became the choke point Ask most operators what will bottleneck AI infrastructure and you'll hear GPUs, transformers, switchgear. NTT Global Data Centers’ stress test suggests something more mundane: paperwork, planning and process. Power availability and deployment timelines, not fiber capacity, are the gating factors in the scenarios modeled. Berti puts it plainly: it doesn't matter how quickly you can get GPUs if you can't get a permit to put them anywhere. That reframes the strategy question. Berti argues against a "build, baby, build" reflex, preferring a portfolio approach that treats capacity expansion as a system-wide coordination problem rather than a land race. The misconceptions that stall projects Two objections come up in almost every community consultation, according to Berti: data centers waste water, and they steal power from the grid. Both are misconceptions and come from an older generation of facilities. Modern designs, he says, use liquid cooling technology, which removes heat more effectively, eliminating excess water waste. Additionally, operators plan the new class of hundred-megawatt-plus sites in partnership with utilities years in advance, often with on-site solar, wind or other renewable generation that can help stabilize the grid rather than drain it. His conclusion is blunt: transparency builds trust. So, the industry has to stop treating what it does as a secret and start to build that trust through education and partnership if it wants the permits it will need through the decade to turn capacity into reliable AI infrastructure that can benefit communities, policymakers and businesses alike. Sponsored by NTT Global Data Centers.

item.title: Customs deepens security partnerships to combat smuggling, protect revenue
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Cross River/Calabar Free Trade Zone/Akwa Ibom Area Command, has intensified efforts to combat smuggling, strengthen border and maritime security, and facilitate legitimate trade through closer collaboration with security agencies and private-sector operators. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Deputy Comptroller, Dr Nkiru Nwala, led delegations to the 13 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Eastern Naval Command, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and Shoreline Logistics Nigeria Limited on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, to strengthen institutional relationships and improve operational coordination. The engagements focused on intelligence sharing, coordinated enforcement operations, protection of critical national assets, road safety, maritime security and compliance with Customs regulations. Speaking during the visits, Nwala emphasised the need for sustained cooperation among security agencies to address smuggling and other criminal activities, protect government revenue and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. She noted that the geographical characteristics of the Command’s operational environment, which encompasses land borders, coastal communities and maritime routes, made collaboration particularly important in tackling illicit activities and emerging security threats. At the 13 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, the Customs delegation was received by the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General P.O. Alimikhena. The discussions highlighted the strategic importance of cooperation in securing border areas, combating smuggling and protecting the nation’s territorial integrity. The Customs delegation stressed that intelligence sharing, timely communication and coordinated enforcement operations would strengthen the effectiveness of both agencies and improve security across the region. Similarly, at the Eastern Naval Command, where the delegation was received on behalf of the Flag Officer Commanding by the Chief of Staff, Rear Admiral S. Ibrahim, Nwala underscored the complementary responsibilities of Customs and the Nigerian Navy in securing the country’s maritime environment. She noted that closer collaboration was necessary to prevent the exploitation of waterways for smuggling and other illicit activities, while strengthening maritime enforcement and protecting legitimate trade. The engagement also highlighted the need for effective communication and operational coordination between the two agencies to address emerging challenges in the coastal and maritime environment. Nwala highlighted the importance of cooperation in addressing security challenges, protecting critical national assets and ensuring the effective discharge of the agencies’ respective statutory responsibilities. item.title: 2027: Hashim Movement targets 3m votes in South-West
item.description: By Clifford Ndujihe The South-West Coordinator of the Gbenga Hashim Solidarity Movement (GHSM), Alhaji Abass Olaniyi, says the movement is targeting more than three million votes for the Accord Party’s presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, across the region in the 2027 general election. Olaniyi said the target was based on the movement’s internal assessment of its grassroots mobilisation prospects across the six South-West states, with Osun, Lagos and Oyo expected to account for a significant share of the projected votes. According to him, Osun State is projected to contribute more than one million votes, while Lagos and Oyo are expected to deliver a combined 1.5 million votes. He said Ogun, Ondo and Ekiti states would contribute the remaining votes needed to achieve the regional target. Olaniyi expressed confidence in the movement’s ability to expand its grassroots presence through engagement with community leaders, youth groups, political stakeholders and local organisations across the region. He also said the movement expected voters in Osun to make independent choices in the presidential election, irrespective of political alignments involving state-level leaders. The coordinator’s projection comes amid preparations by political parties and support groups for the 2027 general election. GHSM said it intended to translate its mobilisation efforts across the South-West into electoral support for Olawepo-Hashim and the Accord Party.
